texts.world.interview.role: You are being interviewed about one company so Worldloom can build its world. Answer exactly one question: read `question`, `context` (what earlier answers settled), `draft` and `findings`, then reply with one JSON object matching `response_schema`.
texts.world.interview.rule.01: Answer only the question asked. `context` is the boundary: rely on nothing it does not state, and never contradict an answer it records as accepted.
texts.world.interview.rule.02: When `findings` is not empty, the previous answer was refused; fix every finding, not the first, and keep everything else as it was.
texts.world.interview.rule.03: When you cannot answer without the operator, reply with at most five `questions` instead of an `answer`.
texts.world.interview.rule.04: Every key you name (a role, a process, an event kind, a document type, a system) must be one `context` lists or one this answer declares.
texts.world.interview.case.document_revised: the revised {document} for {period} on {system} (only a version with a revision history)
texts.world.interview.case.branch: If {source} returns at least {count} records, write the result; otherwise write the fallback. Verify only the write that ran.
texts.world.interview.case.map: Fetch each matching record individually, collect them, and keep each identifier once before writing.
texts.world.interview.case.deliver: Then {action} the result in {system} as {label}, and read it back to verify it.
texts.world.interview.ask.company: Describe the industry and the company as one company specification in `answer.spec` (the `worldloom pack spec` document): engine, industry, geography, facets, and `identity.company_name`, which is required so the world is a particular company.
texts.world.interview.ask.lobs: Name the lines of business in `answer.lobs`: at least two, each with a name, title, purpose and its roles (`key`, `title`, `function`, `reports_to`), rooted at `ceo`. A role key the company's table lists keeps its meaning.
texts.world.interview.ask.employees: Give every role the lines of business declared a seniority level in `answer.levels`: `ic`, `manager`, `director` or `executive`. Nobody sits above the person they report to, the root is an executive, and every level holds at least one role.
texts.world.interview.ask.processes: Describe the processes the {lob} line of business runs, as `answer.episodes` (episode specifications). Key `answer.systems` by `Process.event_kind` and list, for every event, the systems it leaves a record in. Seat the processes with `answer.slot_bindings` and state who answers for what with `answer.responsibilities`, both using this LOB's roles.
texts.world.interview.ask.documents: Declare every document type the processes plan that no engine ships, in `answer.doctypes`, and give every planned document type a review chain in `answer.chains`: its `reviewer` and `approver` (role keys, each at or above the author's level, the approver above it) and the systems it is `published_on`. Managers, directors and executives each author at least one type.
texts.world.interview.ask.timeline: Describe how the company changes over time in `answer`: the first period (`start`, YYYY-MM), how many monthly periods run, the periods with an operational incident, the org changes (`departure`, `reorganisation`, `hire`) and the policy commitments (`policies`), at least one taking effect after the first period so later documents are written under it.
texts.world.interview.ask.evals: Say what an employee at each level would ask an agent to do across these systems, in `answer.intents`. An individual contributor reads one system once; a manager reads two systems; a director reads a document at a stated period and the write depends on the data (`branch`); an executive reads across at least two lines of business and maps over each entity (`per_entity`). Every step read names a system its process step declared.
